overview: This three-document file traces the brief administrative career of Maxwell E. Becker as an engineering adviser in a State Department-sponsored group during the early postwar occupation. Although filed under Japanese internal affairs and titled “Japan, Engineering Adviser,” the surviving communications concern Becker’s appointment, Army travel arrangements, financial preparations for service in Korea, and the final settlement of his salary through the U.S. Political Adviser in Seoul. Together, the January, February, and October 1946 messages show the coordination among the State Department, the Army, and occupation authorities required to recruit, transport, and pay American civilian specialists.

subfiles.title: Telegram confirming Becker’s appointment as engineering adviser
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Martin, Department of State
subfiles.about: The State Department confirms Becker’s appointment and promises further instructions about pay and Army-arranged travel.
subfiles.summary: Martin informs Becker that his appointment was approved effective January 1 and that a formal appointment letter would follow. Becker is asked to specify where his salary checks should be sent. The adviser group is expected to depart shortly once the Army determines the travel arrangements, and Arthur C. Bunce is described as anxious for Becker to remain with the group despite the delay.

subfiles.title: Secret telegram on financial and travel arrangements for Korea
subfiles.from: Edwin M. Martin, Department of State
subfiles.to: Maxwell E. Becker (inferred from context and address)
subfiles.about: The State Department gives Becker financial, permit, and scheduling instructions for his journey to Korea.
subfiles.summary: Although the OCR is badly garbled, the telegram advises that Becker will need only a small amount of cash for incidental expenses during the trip to Korea. It discusses the routing of salary or military checks, indicates that per diem or other expenses will be paid in Korea, and states that no military permit is necessary. Departure from the United States was expected to be scheduled during February.

subfiles.title: Airgram requesting Becker’s final salary-payment letter
subfiles.from: Department of State, signed Byrnes; Acheson also named
subfiles.about: The Department instructs the political adviser in Seoul to submit the documentation required for Becker’s final salary payment.
subfiles.summary: The Department requests a final salary-payment letter for Maxwell E. Becker under the cited provisions of Chapter V of the applicable administrative regulations. The letter is to be submitted to the Payroll Section of the Division of Finance. The airgram was prepared on October 16 and sent on October 18, 1946.

interest: The file offers a compact administrative history of a civilian technical adviser’s service, following Becker from appointment through overseas deployment preparations to final payroll clearance. It is particularly useful for showing how the State Department and Army divided responsibility for transportation, permits, expenses, and salary during the early occupation period. The Korean destination of all the substantive travel and payroll correspondence, despite the file’s placement under a Japanese engineering-adviser classification, also illustrates the sometimes imperfect fit between the decimal filing system and the actual subject matter of individual records.
